properties.name: The schema serves what tells the types apart — after the routing table's own contradiction was fixed
properties.rationale:
flo2 F24, on Anthony's word of 2026-09-22. Recorded as `corrected_cause` because the rules now live where a consumer already reads, with a gate that stops the two records drifting — not a note asking somebody to remember.

⭐ THE ORDER IS THE FINDING. Lifting the table into data exposed that it contradicted itself: row 1 routed "it must never…" to Requirement, row 7 routed "we must never…" to Constraint in bold as "Not a Requirement", so the routing turned on the PRONOUN. flo2's sentence — "the water can never drop below 68 degrees" — has the thing as its subject, so it matched row 1 and the table itself sent it to the wrong type. Serving the table unchanged would have propagated that to every consumer at once, with more confidence than before. The rules had to be RIGHT before being SERVED, and F24's own cause ("they are not served as data") was true but not sufficient.

The correction uses the distinction capture-intent already states two paragraphs below its own table: a Requirement states what must be DELIVERED, a Constraint BOUNDS what is allowed, and the subject of the sentence is irrelevant. Row 1 now carries delivery phrasings only; prohibition and limit phrasings belong to Constraint whoever the sentence is about.

WHY A GATE AND NOT A NOTE. Serving the rules put one contract in two places, which is the BL-159 defect this project has already paid for once. The gate checks both directions and refuses to pass having checked nothing. It earned its place immediately: on its first run, unseeded, it caught two cue phrases written into the schema and not into the table.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, and it is the other half of the same field report: `prohibition_in_prose`'s six phrasings are all built on MUST or on ALLOWED/FORBIDDEN and cover no CAN, so "can never", "cannot", "may not" and "shall not" all miss — which is why flo2's sentence was invisible to the detector as well as misrouted by the table. Different cause, different fix, deliberately not bundled: widening a detector's vocabulary changes what it reports across the whole design and is the owner's call.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `NodeTypeDef` gains `discrimination` (cues, confused_with[type, why], counter_example), carried through `NodeTypeSpec` so `describe_schema` serves it on both the whole-vocabulary and per-type reads. Eight routed types filled in from capture-intent's routing table: Requirement, Capability, Component, Interface, Flow, Constraint, Artifact, DesignRule. The table itself was CORRECTED first. `tools/check_discrimination_rules.py` is wired into the core CI job and listed in AGENTS.md's gate block, and the skill mirrors under .claude/ and .grok/ were resynced.
